Why buildings used to stand inside each other

A duplicated corner made the separator do nothing

When two plots overlapped, the parceller cut the newer one back along an edge of the older. Clipping leaves duplicate corners wherever a vertex lands exactly on the cut line, and a duplicate is a zero-length edge with no direction — so the cut direction came out as (0,0), the inside test dot(0,p) ≤ 0 held for the entire plane, and the “cut” returned the plot whole. It then won the largest-area contest against every real cut, because removing nothing is always biggest. 532 of 1 156 cuts separated nothing.

Three massing paths measured the box, not the plot

Frontage plots are trapezoids, but the courtyard carve, the round tower and the rowhouse terrace each sized themselves from the plot’s bounding box and then checked only that they cleared the road — never that they stayed on their own plot, so they overhung the neighbour. The house path already shrank-to-fit and documents the trap; the other three now do the same.
